# ===========================================================================
# Arkansas SB 8 (Act 154 of the 2026 Fiscal Session, JAR104)
# Source bill id: 2026_2026_4_3_2_000051_0_8_1_20260501_0
#
# Bug: a thin horizontal "leader" rule on page 2 ran from the end of the
# ``(16)     ADMINISTRATIVE SPECIALIST`` label across whitespace into the
# Maximum-No.-of-Employees column.  The rule incidentally overlapped the
# trailing "2" by ~6pt and was misclassified as an underline by
# :func:`_classify_char_decoration`, producing the false
# ``[A>2<A]`` tag the user reported in the screenshot.
#
# Fix: :func:`_filter_ar_leader_lines` (Arkansas-only) drops horizontal
# rules whose horizontal extent is covered < 50 % by text on their
# baseline.  In this bill, real legislative underlines covered 69-100 %
# of the line's extent while leaders covered 0-35 %, so the 50 %
# threshold cleanly separates them.
#
# This fixture locks the fix in TWO directions:
#   1. The salary-row digit must remain plain text ("       2     ").
#   2. Genuine legislative additions (SECTION 13 emergency clause,
#      underlined dollar amounts, underlined year labels) must keep
#      their [A>…<A] tags.
# ===========================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Forbidden: tags that were emitted before the fix and must stay stripped.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The headline bug: a bare "2" in the salary-table employee column.
![A>2<A]

# A bare "3" tagged on page 3 in the same column for another row.
![A> 3<A]

# A bare "0" tagged in another row's employee column.
![A>            0<A]

# Page-wide column-header leader rules — text "NO." / "Title" /
# "Employees" / "2026-2027" were misread as one giant addition because
# the underlying rule spans the whole page width but only touches the
# four label strings.
![A> NO.     Title                               Employees          2026-2027<A]
![A> NO.                                                             2026-2027<A]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Required: real legislative additions that MUST still be tagged.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The ADMINISTRATIVE SPECIALIST salary row.  The "2" must be plain text,
# but the rest of the row must extract verbatim.  Note the whitespace
# layout is what the extractor emits; if the geometry changes this line
# is the canary that catches it.
(16)     ADMINISTRATIVE SPECIALIST       2     $48,575

# Genuine underlined dollar amounts on page 3 / 4 / 5 (real underlines,
# coverage 69-84 %) — must remain inside [A>…<A] tags.
[A> $3,438,833<A]
[A> $3,824,800<A]
[A> $50,002,500<A]
[A> $2,500,500<A]

# Genuine underlined year labels on page 5 (coverage 99-100 %) — these
# are short hlines that hug the year text; the filter must not strip them.
[A>2026<A]
[A>2027<A]

# Genuine STRIKETHROUGH year labels on page 5 — these sit at the
# characters' midline, NOT at the baseline.  Pre-2026-06-29 the AR
# leader-line filter only checked baseline proximity, so it counted
# 0% text coverage on strikethrough hlines and dropped them as if
# they were leaders.  The resulting output showed plain "2025" /
# "2026" instead of [D>2025<D] / [D>2026<D] inside the Section 9 / 10
# date-range clauses.  Fix: _filter_ar_leader_lines now accepts a
# character as "text-bearing" when the hline y falls anywhere within
# the character's vertical bbox (strikethrough geometry) OR within
# baseline_tol pt below the baseline (underline geometry).
[D>2025<D]
[D>2026<D]

# The "through June 30" half of the date-range clause is rendered on
# a single physical PDF line, so its full tagged form is a stable
# substring.  Pin BOTH the strikethrough (`[D>2026<D]`) and the
# adjacent underline (`[A>2027<A]`) so the strikethrough-detection
# fix is verified end-to-end alongside the existing
# underline-detection guarantee.
through June 30, [D>2026<D] [A>2027<A].

# The "from July 1" half is split across a physical line break in
# the PDF (the strikethrough year falls on the next visible line
# below "from July 1,"), but the adjacency of the strikethrough +
# underline pair survives consolidation on the second occurrence
# (Section 10).  This is the strongest single-line proof that BOTH
# decorations were detected on the same row.
[D>2025<D] [A>2026<A] through June 30, [D>2026<D] [A>2027<A].

# Section 13 emergency clause — entirely underlined as a single
# multi-line legislative addition (coverage 81-88 %).  We pin the
# distinctive opening and the final clause as canaries; the filter
# preserves both.
[A>SECTION 13. EMERGENCY CLAUSE. It is found and determined by the<A]
[A>and safety shall be in full force and effect from and after July 1, 2026.<A]
